input.subject: Update: Unit 14 (Tanya Mitchell) — Balance, Eviction Status & Make-Ready
input.body:
Dear Mr. Harris,

I'm writing to give you a current, verified update on the delinquency and eviction matter for your tenant Tanya Mitchell (Unit 14).

OUTSTANDING BALANCE
As of today, Ms. Mitchell's verified outstanding balance is $2,287.50, made up of:
  • Carried-forward rent arrears: $1,125.00
  • June rent: $975.00
  • Late fees (through the cure deadline): $187.50

The payment plan we had put in place was breached when she missed the June 23 installment, and no payments have been received since — so the full balance above stands. I reconciled this figure directly against our accounting records before sending it to you.

EVICTION STATUS
  • A 3-day notice to pay or quit was served on or about June 28. The cure deadline (June 29) passed with no payment and no contact from Ms. Mitchell.
  • The filing package (lease, rent ledger, notice history, and authorization) is assembled, and we are filing the eviction (forcible detainer) petition with the Justice of the Peace court today, July 1.
  • To set expectations clearly: the petition is being filed now — a hearing has not yet taken place. Once filed, the JP court will set a hearing date; if we prevail, the court issues a judgment for possession, followed by a writ of possession before we can regain the unit. I will keep you updated at each step.

UNIT AVAILABILITY / MAKE-READY
  • The unit cannot be turned or re-marketed yet. Ms. Mitchell remains in legal possession until the eviction is completed and the unit is vacated.
  • We have placed the make-ready on hold and will not schedule any turnover work or advertise the unit until we have legal possession — this avoids committing costs prematurely or marketing a unit we cannot yet deliver.

I'll follow up as soon as the court sets a hearing date. Please don't hesitate to reach out with any questions in the meantime.

Best regards,
Patricia Nguyen
Property Manager
Star Property Management

Everything's done. Here's the full picture, Patricia — and a few things that came back different from what you'd assumed.

## 1. What Tanya actually owes: **$2,287.50**

Walked back to the underlying charges (verified in QuickBooks against the consolidated eviction-filing ledger, invoice #7214):

| Component | Amount |
|---|---|
| Carried-forward rent arrears (May) | $1,125.00 |
| June rent | $975.00 |
| Late fees (through the 6/29 cure deadline) | $187.50 |
| **Verified outstanding** | **$2,287.50** |

**⚠️ This is where your assumption was off — and it's exactly the trap you flagged.** The back rent was *not* squared away. That same ledger invoice also carries a **$5,885.94 "partial payment plan credit" line** and shows a **$0.00 balance**. Both are junk:
- There are **zero payment records and zero credit memos** on her account in QuickBooks. Nothing was ever paid under the plan.
- The ledger's own note says the account **"remains delinquent with no cure received."**
- The $0.00 balance and the $8,173.44 invoice total are data-entry artifacts (the "credit" was keyed as a positive charge line, and every line's item type is mislabeled).

If you'd taken the invoice at face value you'd have either put $0.00 (double-counting a credit that doesn't exist) or $8,173.44 into the filing. **The clean, defensible number is $2,287.50** — full charges, no legitimate credit to net against it.

## 2. Where the eviction actually stands

**Also off from your memory — we are *not* past the hearing stage. We're only reaching the *filing* stage today.**

- 3-day notice served ~**June 28**; cure deadline **June 29** passed with no payment and no contact → record moved to "Notice Expired."
- The petition has **NOT been filed yet.** The **JP Court eviction-filing appointment is this afternoon (July 1, 4:30 pm CT)**; Airtable tracking = "Filing in Progress."
- **What comes next:** file the forcible-detainer petition today → JP sets a hearing → judgment for possession if we prevail → writ of possession before we get the unit back.
- The **May "hearing set / favorable ruling expected"** thread on OPS-32 (and the May 13 "court hearing" calendar entry) **predates the June notice and filing steps and appears premature** — you can't have had a real FED hearing before the petition was even filed. Treat that May track as a false start, not history.

**Owner authorization — this needs your attention before it goes into the court file:** The authorization on record (EVF-2026-014, 6/30) is from **Linda Castillo**. But the Linear eviction issue OPS-32 consistently frames this as **Harry Harris's** unit (Harry as owner/witness, owner-side updates to Harry). **Both are listed as "Property Owner" in Contacts**, and HubSpot's owner link for Tanya is contaminated (points to a carpet vendor), so it can't break the tie. **Confirm who actually owns Unit 14 before you file / before the owner email goes** — if it's Harris, the Castillo authorization is the wrong owner's.

**One more:** the unit is labeled inconsistently across systems — **4B / 214 / Sunset Ridge Unit 14**. Nail down the official designation for the petition; a wrong unit ID on a court filing is a problem.

**FYI (not for the owner email):** an approved **ESA reasonable-accommodation addendum** is on file for Tanya. That doesn't block a nonpayment eviction, but keep the case strictly nonpayment-based so there's no retaliation/pretext angle.

## 3. Can we release the unit for make-ready? **No — hold it.**

Tenant is still in **legal possession**; there's been no move-out (the 6/29 date was the notice cure deadline, not a move-out). No turnover work, no vendors, and no marketing until the eviction concludes and the unit is legally vacated.

## What I updated
- **Airtable make-ready:** Updated the "Unit 14 – Tanya Mitchell Eviction" record to the real current state (occupied, petition being filed today, **ON HOLD**), cleared the misleading 6/29 move-out date and stale target-ready date, and logged the open items. Did the same on a **duplicate** eviction-track record I found (flagged it as a dup pointing to the primary).
- **OPS-32 (Linear):** Added a status-reconciliation note covering the balance, filing stage, owner conflict, unit-ID discrepancy, and make-ready hold.
- **#make-ready (Slack):** Posted a hold/heads-up so nobody mobilizes.
- **Owner email:** Drafted (in your Gmail drafts, addressed to Harry Harris) covering the $2,287.50 balance, eviction status, and the make-ready hold — **but confirm the correct owner before sending**, given the Castillo/Harris conflict above.

Nothing was filed or sent on your behalf — the email is a draft for your review, and the JP filing is your appointment this afternoon.
